turns.text: Hey Lloyd, did you fix that bug with the login screen?
Yes, I pushed the hotfix. Can you verify it on your end?

Just checked, looks good. By the way, I'm running some experiments with GWM-Robotics today. It's surprisingly affordable to run the physics simulation itself, but human grading is the expensive part. We're using about 10 graders per rollout, which is killing our budget.
That sounds like a significant bottleneck. Have you considered automating the grading process?
Not yet. The current model requires human judgment for nuance. Anyway, I need to go. Can you order me a new mouse? The scroll wheel is broken again.
Sure, I'll order a Logitech MX Master 3S. Anything else?
Lloyd, what's the weather like for Saturday's hiking trip?
It looks sunny with highs around 75°F. Perfect hiking weather.

Great. Speaking of things I'm working on, I've been digging deeper into GWM-Robotics. It's essentially an offline proxy for robot policy evaluation using general world models. That context helps explain why the simulation isn't the cost driver.
That makes sense. Offline proxies can significantly reduce the compute load compared to live deployment.
Exactly. Also, did you confirm the dinner reservation for 7 PM?
Yes, it's confirmed for two at the Italian place downtown.
